title.narrative: Strengthening the National Statistical System of Zambia
Stärkande av det nationella statistiksystemet i Zambia

description.narrative:
Ambassaden har mottagit en gemensam projektansökan från Zambia Statistics Agency (Zamstats) och Statistiska Centralbyrån (SCB) med namnet "Increased access to statistics that are relevant to meet user needs". Projektetförslaget har en total budget på SEK 44 434 000 och är resultat av en förberedelsefas som genomförts av de två organisationerna under perioden februari till juli 2019 och som finansierades av Ambassaden med en budget av SEK 1 183 000.
Den föreslagna insatsen kommer att genomföras gemensamt av Zamstats och SCB under perioden 2019 - 2023. Projektmålet är att användarna har ökad tillgång till oberoende, tillförlitlig och högkvalitativ statistik som publiceras i god tid, är korrekt och relevant och möter användarnas efterfrågan och behov. Projektet är indelat i fyra komponenter. Den första är Koordinering och det förväntade resultatet är ett stärkt system för nationell statistik (NSS). Den andra komponenten är Statistikproduktion och det förväntade resultatet är en förbättrad omfattning och kvalitet av Zamstats statistikproduktion. Den tredje komponenten är Kommunikation och spridning och det förväntade resultatet är ökad tillgång till och förståelse hos användare av statistik. Den fjärde komponenten är ICT och det förväntade resultatet är en existerande ICT-miljö som stödjer effektiv statistikproduktion.

The Embassy has received a joint project proposal from Zambia Statistics Agency and Statistics Sweden called "Increased access to statistics that are relevant to meet user needs". The proposal has a total budget of SEK 44 434 000 and is the outcome of a scoping phase implemented by Zamstats and Statistics Sweden between February and July 2019 and financed by the Embassy with a budget of SEK 1 183 000.
The proposed contribution is a collaboration between the Zambia Statistics Agency and Statistics Sweden over the period 2019 - 2023. The objective of the project is that users have increased access to unbiased, reliable and quality statistics that are timely, accurate and relevant to meet their needs. The project is divided into four project components. The first component is Coordination and the expected outcome is a strengthened National Statistical System. The second component is Statistical Production and the expected outcome is improved range and quality of Zamstats’ statistical production. The third component is Communication and Dissemination and the expected outcome is increased user access and improved user understanding of existing statistics. The fourth component is Information and Communication Technology and the expected outcome is an ICT environment in place that supports efficient statistics production.

Long-term outcome (impact) The project shall contribute to, together with other development interventions, that Policy makers in Zambia use unbiased, reliable and quality information to design polices that contribute to a sustainable development of the country. Project Objective Users have increased access to unbiased, reliable and quality statistics that are timely, accurate and relevant to meet user needs Component outcomes 1. Coordination: Strengthened National Statistical System 2. Statistical production: Improved range and quality of CSO’s statistical production 3. Communication and dissemination: Increased user access and improved user understanding of existing statistics 4. Information and Communication Technology: An ICT environment in place that supports efficient statistics production

title.narrative: Agreement Statistics Sweden Strengthening the National Statistical System of Zambia
Decision on Contribution Statistics Sweden Strengthening the National Statistical System of Zambia

description.narrative:
Examples of results achieved:
Component 1: Coordination - The expected outcome of the component is a Strengthened National Statistical System.
The broader National Statistical System showed increased trust and engagement with ZamStats during this period. The National Statistical Coordinating Committee (NSCC) and National Technical Working Groups (NTWGs) continued to operate regularly, and ministries demonstrated increased willingness to participate and coordinate with ZamStats, showing a shift toward more collaborative production of official statistics across government. Development and printing of a Code of Practice for Official Statistics in Zambia in line with ZamStats' responsibilities under the Statistics Act. The Code of Practice shall govern the quality of official statistics in Zambia across the statistical system. Publication of the National Statistics Realise calendar (NSRC) for 2025. ZamStats finalized the National Data Science Training Hub, marking a major step toward long-term sustainability in statistical capacity development. The centre provides a permanent institutional platform for training ZamStats staff and the wider National Statistical System, enabling continuous delivery of STAC courses, methodological training, and data science skills development.
Component 2: Statistical Production The expected outcome of the component is Improved range and quality of ZamStats statistical production.
ZamStats technical capacity has improved significantly through the institutionalization of modern statistical methods, by using NADABAS as the new structured calculation system. By using NADABAS and initiating the GDP rebasing process, ZamStats have modernized GDP compilation, updated the benchmark year and strengthened economic statistics quality. ZamStats strengthened its internal methodological governance through operationalizing the Methodology and Standards Committee established in 2024, enabling better harmonization across all statistical production. ZamStats further strengthened its work on environmental and climate statistics through a stakeholder meeting in early 2025, that identified data gaps and integrated an environmental model into the Household Budget Survey to collect new data on waste management. ZamStats further strengthened its methodological expertise through the completion of the second phase of advanced methodology training in 2025. Increased the basic statistical capacities in Zambia by STAC course, primarily for the NTWG on Environment.
Component 3: Communication and Dissemination The expected outcome of the component is Increased user access and improved user understanding of existing statistics.
The component has had challenges in implementing the planned activities. Although the development of the communication strategy did not take off at the stipulated time, the ZamStats communication team produced and submitted the draft communication strategy to ZamStats management. The collaboration with other agencies and ministries through establishment coordination mechanisms such as the NSCC, NTWG and STAC courses has led to improved knowledge within the NSS about ZamStats' areas of responsibilities and key competencies.
Component 4: Information & Communication Technology The expected outcome of the) component is "An ICT environment in place that supports efficient statistics production".
ZamStats drafted an Information Security Management System (ISMS) strategy and policy. The procurement process of laptops and computers commenced to ensure ZamStats staff are provided with corporate laptops. The ICT Strategy and Policy Framework, was approved by the board in the first quarter of 2025, providing clear priorities for ICT investment, guidance for data security and a strategic ground for future ICT development. Quality Reports have been further integrated into routine work among staff strengthening credibility and transparency.
Component 5: Management the project aimed to support managers to understand the staffs motivation so that they can align the individual needs with the interests of the organisation, and by that create sustainable change that benefits both the staff and the organisation.
This was done during benchmarking with Statistics South Africa and Statistics Sweden. The learning enabled management at ZamStats to plan for an establishment of a statistical business model to guide the operations of the agency. Also, more interaction and weekly planning meetings by management is a result of inclusion of this component in the project.
Management reforms have advanced, including the first activity of the Generic Statistical Business Process Model (GSBPM) in January 2025, which is a shift toward more standardized, process based production of statistics.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
